text:
Jules R: Morning team — quick async standup for gateway/routing. Did a tiny canary of the routing-policy v2 (subset of traffic -> new auth header flow). Saw a few 503s hitting /v1/chat during a short burst. Pasting concise notes below — will follow up with runbook updates.

Priya P: thanks Jules. do you have a request_id or short log so I can correlate with auth service?

Jules R: request_id=0f4c9a; log snippet: ```ERROR gateway/handler.go:142 response=503 upstream=chat-svc-2 conn=short-lived kv=cache-miss``` Also saw 429s from the canary to the backend a minute earlier.

Ben C: pinging infra now — will check pool saturation and kube pod restarts. Quick hypothesis: burst handling + new header causing route match thrash, backend pool sees short spikes.

ci-bot: Deployment notice — gw-config v2-canary started by Jules R at 2026-03-16T22:14:03Z :rocket:

Marco L: if auth header changes the mapping, we might be falling back to legacy route which has lower capacity. PR #438 updates the extractor. Marco -> https://github.com/redwood/gateway/pull/438 for context.

Priya P: I can review PR#438 after this thread. Suggest temporary mitigation: reduce canary percentage to 10% and raise per-route burst limit from 200 to 400 tokens/sec for the next 30m so we can get signal without backend overload. Command to patch canary: `kubectl patch canary gw-config -p '{"spec":{"traffic":10}}'`

Jules R: good call. lowered traffic to 10% and increased burst limit via the policy UI. Also toggled auth-strict=false on the canary to allow legacy fallthrough.

Ben C: checked metrics — two pods in chat-svc-2 hit 98% socket wait for ~30s then recovered. Opening an incident-ish note in incidents channel if we see another spike. Added link to dashboard: https://grafana.redwood/influx/gw-canary-surge

Marco L: I'll add a lightweight heartbeat to the route (emit route_version tag) so we can tell which backend handled requests in logs. Quick diff in the PR.

Priya P: Reviewing PR now — small nits but nothing blocking. Able to approve if we add one test for header-preservation.

Jules R: blockers: can't reproduce 503 locally (LM: env parity). Need Ben to confirm whether backend pools are evicting connections under the new header. Today: 1) tail canary logs for 1h, 2) run a focused load test against canary at 10% traffic, 3) merge PR#438 after Priya approval and roll a tiny canary again.

Ben C: started a focused load test using `loadtest --rps 300 --duration 5m /v1/chat` against canary IPs. Will post results in ~6m.

ci-bot: Canary pipeline smoke-check queued by Ben C — job id smoke-7721.

Priya P: thumbs up on the plan. small reminder: update the rollout doc with the throttle rollback step.

Jules R: done — updated /runbooks/gateway-canary.md with rollback snippet and the new metric to watch (route_version and socket_wait_ms).

Marco L: noted. I'll also add a Prometheus rule to alert if socket_wait_ms > 200ms for >1m.

Ben C: load test done — saw a short tail of 503s at minute 2 but recovered; socket_wait_ms peaked at 260ms on two pods. Captured logs and attached to thread.

Jules R: thanks. next steps: Priya approves PR -> merge -> small canary bump to 25% for 15m. If no regression, proceed to 50%. If anyone sees >1% 5xx in that window, rollback to previous policy via the UI.

Priya P: approved PR#438, adding a quick unit test in a follow-up.

Marco L: I'll ship the heartbeat and the alert rule in a follow-up PR today.

Jules R: awesome — thanks all. If you need me ping `@JulesR` here. :thumbsup: 

Ben C: looping in infra-oncall if escalation needed.

ci-bot: Note: automatic rollback threshold set to 1% 5xx for canary.

Jules R: closing the loop — I'll post a short postmortem if anything persists. For now, monitoring and incremental rollouts.
